ai.description: Nikhil’s Kukri Snake reaches 30–40 cm. It is reddish-brown with a distinct dark nuchal collar and a series of dark, light-edged dorsal blotches. A prominent dark stripe runs through each eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Oligodon nikhili* is best distinguished by the unique presence of a distinct, V-shaped dark marking on the nape, which is absent in other similar Indian kukri snakes.
ai.habitat: Nikhil's Kukri Snake inhabits the high-altitude evergreen forests and shola grasslands of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations above 1,500 meters.
ai.behavior: Nikhil’s Kukri Snake is primarily nocturnal, using its specialized, blade-like teeth to slice through and feed on the eggs of other reptiles.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Oligodon nikhili* is oviparous, laying a clutch of 3–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the pre-monsoon season, with hatchlings appearing by late summer.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Oligodon nikhili* is endemic to the southern Western Ghats in Kerala, India, where it inhabits high-elevation montane forests at approximately 1,500 meters.
